name: Conjunction Density & Parataxis Deficit
description: Measures the frequency of coordinating and subordinating conjunctions relative to the total word count to detect hyper-connective synthetic writing.
algorithm: Syntactic Linkage Profiling & Conjunction Ratio Calculation
mechanism: Large Language Models are explicitly optimized for logical cohesion and readability. To ensure maximum clarity, they obsessively link clauses using explicit conjunctions ('and', 'but', 'because', 'although', 'while'). They rarely trust the reader to infer relationships between sentences. Human writers, however, frequently employ 'parataxis'—the technique of placing clauses side by side without connecting words (e.g., 'It was raining. We stayed inside.')—relying on context and implicit logical leaps. This method parses the Parts-Of-Speech (POS) tags of the text to calculate the strict ratio of conjunctions to total words. An abnormally high conjunction density indicates a 'hyper-connective' AI that is algorithmically incapable of leaving logical joints unarticulated, resulting in overly smooth, synthetically flowing prose.
useCase: Identifying artificially fluid articles, essays, and stories where the AI over-explains relationships between clauses rather than allowing natural narrative fragmentation.
strengths:
• Highly effective at capturing the 'overly smooth' feeling of AI text that humans struggle to articulate but intuitively sense.
• Robust against simple vocabulary swapping, as it targets the fundamental syntactic glue of the text.
• Fast and computationally inexpensive, relying on lightweight POS tagging.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing highly technical, legal, or instructional human texts where explicit logical connections are strictly required.
• Performance drops on very short texts where conjunction variance is statistically meaningless.
• An expert prompter can bypass this by explicitly demanding 'choppy, fragmented sentences' or 'asyndeton'.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tag Counting & Syntactic Linkage
Metric: Conjunction:Word Ratio (Density per 100 words)
Output: 0-100 Hyper-Connectivity (Conjunction Overuse) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85%. Works best as a supporting metric alongside sentence length variance and transition marker analysis.

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
